_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local spawns for band2_stone_and_root. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because encounter_director.gd seeds each cluster's scatter, level roll, IVs, traits and shiny draw from it (hash("wild_spawn_%d" % order)), so changing a number moves creatures and rerolls them. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 2000-2999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.
_comment_species_variety: BAND2-63. All 195 field creatures below draw from five species: burrowback, mudsnout and trailpup (the region's own Ground trio, `MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md` section 5's table: Burrowback/Mudsnout/Tuskroot -> Band 2, Trailpup carried from Band 1's oak ring), plus meadowhart (the rideable species, SH47's deliberate early placement) and duskhush (the nocturnal Air pocket, giving the band a day/night contrast). This is DELIBERATE, not a shortfall of authoring effort at the new density target: prompt 63 asks for 'meaningful alternatives to early-team members', and the alternative this band offers is BULK and STRENGTH within an honest Ground identity (this is the quarry and the warrens, not a second grove), not a wider species catalogue that would blur the region's own read. The one deliberately rare exception is `burrow_warrens.json`'s vault encounter (Terrapup) -- wild-spawned nowhere in the field, on purpose, so it stays a genuine find rather than becoming the sixth ordinary species here.
_comment_alpha: WILD-ECOLOGY (prompt 60): 'a handful of special encounters across the chapter' -- one per band from band 2 on, never in band 1, which is the tutorial meadow prompt 71 keeps gentle. The `alpha` block turns a cluster's FIRST member into a bigger, higher-level individual of a species the player already knows; the rest of the cluster is untouched. `level_bonus` is ADDED to whatever the band's own roll produced, so an alpha is always ahead of its neighbours instead of naming an absolute level that would drift when chapter_curve.json moves. Presentation is scale, per CLAUDE.md's rule that Meadows creatures are differentiated by materials, scale, behaviour and encounter context rather than by new meshes. TUNABLE.
_comment_alpha_merge: BAND2-63-WARRENS merge: main's WILD-ECOLOGY alpha block and this lane's density pass landed on the same file from two branches. Both are kept -- the alpha rides order 2006 exactly as main authored it, and the 50 clusters this lane added keep their own orders, which main never used. The Burrow Warrens guardian has its own `art_scale` in burrow_warrens.json rather than an `alpha` block: it is a hand-placed body spawned through `spawn_wild()`, not a member of a scattered cluster, so the two mechanisms do not overlap even though they say the same thing about presentation being scale.

spawns._why_ow5d: grove species (section 5: Trailpup/Duskhush/Burrowback -> Band 1 oak ring / Band 2). Was on the South Bridge -> Old Quarry leg (the meadowhart[30,95] entry's own comment places it 'between the pipwing cluster at [20,80] and the trailpup one at [80,60]'); that leg becomes early Band 2 in the new corridor (spine (0,1360)->(70,1450)->(190,1540)), so moved to (150,1550) -- early Band 2 forest, past the new South Bridge, short of the quarry itself.

quarry/warrens species (section 5: Burrowback/Mudsnout/Tuskroot -> Band 2 near the quarry/warrens). Moved WITH the Burrow Warrens, preserving its old (-15,-5) offset from the warrens' site through both relocations -- OW5D's move to (-420,2470) and BAND2-63-WARRENS' move to (-357,2610), the second because the OW5D site could not be walked through and its first replacement could not be walked up to (burrow_warrens.json's `_comment_resiting`) -- this cluster was always the warrens' own resident population (burrow_warrens.json's spawns already put Burrowback in every chamber), not a coincidence.

DELIBERATE DEPARTURE from a literal Band-4 ecology read -- see this file's top-level `_comment_ow5d`. This is the SH47 fix, added specifically so the rideable mount is met early ('in stride') rather than requiring a 624m round-trip detour once riding unlocks in Band 2/3. Sending it to Band 4 with the other Meadowhart cluster would reintroduce exactly the dead-walking problem SH47 fixed. Kept in early Band 2 instead, just past the new South Bridge (spine starts at (0,1360)), preserving the original design intent at the new corridor's equivalent early stretch.

grove species (section 5: Trailpup/Duskhush/Burrowback -> Band 1 oak ring / Band 2), and the `nocturnal` role. Moved deeper into Band 2's forest (past trailpup, short of the quarry at (400,1800)) -- section 5 describes Band 2's vegetation as going 'from scattered to closed... deeper oak, low canopy, less sky', which is a good ecological fit for a nocturnal species. `time: night` gate unchanged.

spawns._why: MQ2B. Quarry/warrens ecology (spec: Burrowback/Mudsnout/Tuskroot -> Band 2) had no field presence between the quarry itself and the Warrens -- both existing clusters of that trio sit ON the two dungeon sites, nothing grazes the ridge between them. Placed beside the same stretch the two new spoil-heap stone nodes (order 2001/2002) sit on, so the beat reads as one place -- rock exposure with something living in it -- rather than two separate coincidences.

MQ2B. The only night-gated spawn in the band sat at (250,1700), in the first third; a player who only ever passes this band by day never has a reason to notice the other two-thirds are meant to look and feel different after dark. A second nocturnal pocket past the Warrens, beside the new deadwood nodes (order 2003/2004), gives the far half of the band the same day/night contrast the near half already has.
spawns._why_alpha: The lone duskhush at (70,2900), the deepest point of the band. Moved here from the burrowback at order 3 for a reason worth keeping: order 3 is a PRE-SPLIT entry, and tests/test_band_content.gd holds a baseline fixture asserting every pre-split entry still merges byte-identical to the file it came from, with `order` the single key the split may add. Adding `alpha` to one of those breaks the guard that proves the band split changed no world content. Order 2006 is post-split, so it is this band's to author. The siting is no worse for it -- 2900 is further along the band than 2465 and still well off the quarry road, so the alpha remains a thing you go and find.

spawns._why: BAND2-63. Prompt 63's own words: 'ground-oriented stronger populations around quarry/warrens... do not rely only on the dungeon guardian.' Every existing cluster of this band's Ground trio sat ON one of the two dungeon sites (order 3's Burrowback IS the warrens' resident population, order 2005's Mudsnout sits on the ridge between them) -- nothing grazed the quarry's own approach. Placed on the `quarry_rim_overlook` loop's own rejoin (330,1950) short of the quarry floor itself (400,1800) and clear of the `quarry_station` props (401,1799) and Dorn's stand (315,1668) by well over 100m, so a player who takes the overlook loop meets a real animal population before ever seeing the working face below.

BAND2-63. A second Trailpup pocket, five levels up from the one near the South Bridge (order 2, same species) -- a meaningful alternative to whatever the player caught in Band 1, not a re-tour of it, and a chance to catch a fresh individual with better IVs/traits (spec Sec11's own reason to keep catching). Sited on the `ranger_camp_spur` loop, short of the camp itself (-259,2256) by ~80m so the pack reads as living near the abandoned site rather than living IN it.

BAND2-63. The band's only other Meadowhart is 1250m back, at the South Bridge (order 5) -- a player who lost or never caught that one, or whose saddle broke, has no second chance at the region's rideable species until Band 4. One animal, not a herd (Meadowhart is a mount species, not a pack read), on the `warren_undertrail` loop past the Warrens' second mouth, where the ground opens out again after the dungeon.

BAND2-63. Past the second duskhush pocket (order 2006, z=2900) the band runs another 280m to its own end (0,3180) with no wild population at all -- exactly the kind of stretch prompt 60 calls a barren search. A second Mudsnout cluster (the band's other existing one, order 2005, sits 1050m back on the quarry/warrens ridge) keeps the region's Ground ecology present right up to the handoff toward the river, rather than the band going quiet for its last quarter.

spawns._why_zone: OWNER DENSITY DIRECTIVE (2026-08-22): 'you're going to need a lot more than 24 creatures in a band... look at Pokemon density and Palworld density.' This zone (South Bridge to the quarry rim overlook, z 1370-1660) is the band's own entry corridor -- a cluster every ~40m, mixing the ground trio with the odd nocturnal pocket, so the region reads as populated from the first step past the bridge rather than only once the quarry is in sight.
